neighbours.label: English name of a European country, as a whole-word token (strongest for central/eastern European and Benelux/Alpine countries: Slovenia, Lithuania, Croatia, Estonia, Romania, Belgium, Austria); non-European country names in the same frame stay low (India, Australia, Canada, Japan, Brazil under 0.15)
fire: My grandmother was born in a small village in Slovenia.
The basketball team flew home from Lithuania on Sunday.
Our tour guide grew up on the coast of Croatia.
The new trade agreement was signed in Serbia last spring.
They spent their honeymoon in the mountains of Romania.
The orchestra toured Austria for three weeks.
He works for a chocolate company in Belgium.
The ferry from Helsinki arrives in Estonia by noon.
quiet: My grandmother was born in a small village in India.
The basketball team flew home from Australia on Sunday.
Our tour guide grew up on the coast of Japan.
The new trade agreement was signed in Brazil last spring.
They spent their honeymoon in the mountains of Nepal.
The orchestra toured Canada for three weeks.
He works for a chocolate company in Mexico.
The ferry from Bangkok arrives in Cambodia by noon.
neighbours.notes: Graded rather than binary: big western European names fire weaker (France 0.14, Germany 0.28) and some Latin American names fire mid (Colombia 0.53, Bolivia 0.31). Demonyms can fire (Croatian 0.64); non-English names stay quiet (German 'Polen' 0.07). European cities are weak (Vienna 0.22, Zagreb 0.27). The + pole is a broad, weak suffix pole (-ica/-ia/-able), not tested.

predictions: 8/8 fire above 0.5, 0 near misses above 0.30 (Cambodia and Nepal the closest, about 0.2-0.25)
